clue.text: Capital decoration for best granny?

parts.note: the best is the top, as in top of the class
a granny is a type of knot, the granny knot

explanation.surface: A question about what ornament would suit the finest grandmother.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Capital' here means of the head (Latin caput), not a city or money.
explanation.definitionFit: A topknot is a tuft of hair or ribbon worn on the crown of the head, so a decoration for one's capital.

clue.text: Reduce volume of docking order

definitions.meaning: to diminish or fade away, as sound does
a command to dock an animal, cutting off its tail

explanation.surface: An instruction to turn the sound down when ships come into port.
explanation.walkthrough: 'docking' suggests ships; here it is cutting an animal's tail.
explanation.definitionFit: To tail off is to dwindle; read literally it is a command to remove the tail, as docking does.

clue.text: Heavy exercise not for the anonymous

definitions.text: Heavy exercise not for the anonymous

parts.words: Heavy exercise not for the anonymous
parts.note: a military punishment of marching in full kit, and the old saying 'no names: if no one is named, no one can be punished

explanation.surface: A tough workout that is unsuited to those who stay nameless.
explanation.walkthrough: 'No names, no pack drill' is a British saying meaning that nobody can be blamed if nobody is named.
explanation.definitionFit: Soldiers were punished by marching up and down in full kit with a loaded knapsack.

clue.text: Standard 'A' girl

parts.note: a norm is a standard

explanation.surface: A first-rate young woman, graded top of the standard.
explanation.definitionFit: Norma is a woman's first name.

clue.text: Three bands on display for a Parisian flier

definitions.text: Three bands on display for a Parisian flier

parts.words: Three bands on display for a Parisian flier
parts.note: the French national flag shows three vertical stripes of blue, white and red, and flags fly

explanation.surface: Three musical groups performing for a pilot from Paris.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bands' suggests musicians and 'flier' an aviator; they are stripes and a flag.
explanation.definitionFit: The French flag is a banner of three vertical stripes.

clue.text: Colourful early precursor of the motor car

definitions.text: Colourful early precursor of the motor car

parts.words: Colourful early precursor of the motor car
parts.note: under the old ... Act a man had to walk ahead of early motor vehicles carrying a warning banner, so it literally went before the car

explanation.surface: A history note about some vivid forerunner of the automobile.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Precursor' suggests an invention that came before cars; in fact it is something that walked in front of each car, on British roads in the 19th century.
explanation.definitionFit: Victorian law required a person bearing a crimson warning banner to precede each self-propelled vehicle.

clue.text: Send forward or back

definitions.meaning: to send money or payment on, as in remitting a fee
to send a case back to a lower court, a legal sense

explanation.surface: Instructions to post something on or return it.
explanation.definitionFit: One remits payment by forwarding it, and a judge remits a case by returning it for reconsideration.

clue.text: Run down in trade, for example, after crash

indicators.note: a crash smashes things apart, so the letters are scrambled into a new order

parts.note: EG is the abbreviation for exempli gratia, for example

explanation.surface: Business slumps, for instance, after a financial crash.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crash' sits after its fodder, and the abbreviation for 'for example' joins the shuffled pool. 'Run down' means disparage, not exhausted.
explanation.definitionFit: To denigrate is to belittle or disparage, to criticise unfairly.

clue.text: Cut student article on church

parts.note: L is for learner, as on a British learner driver's plate
an is the indefinite article
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: A pupil's essay about the church gets edited.
explanation.definitionFit: To lance is to pierce a boil with a blade, to make an incision.

clue.text: Scrap collector carrying less weight after middle age

indicators.note: after puts the thinner word behind the letter from age
middle points to the central letter of the word age

parts.note: leaner means slimmer, carrying less body weight

explanation.surface: Someone collecting scraps who has slimmed down past middle age.
explanation.walkthrough: 'middle age' looks like a time of life; it is the middle letter of 'age'.
explanation.definitionFit: A gleaner gathers leftover grain or bits of information after the main harvest.

clue.text: At home, a vicious dog to provoke

parts.note: at home means in, as in 'she is in'
a cur is a nasty or mongrel dog

explanation.surface: A warning that keeping a savage dog in the house invites trouble.
explanation.definitionFit: To incur trouble is to bring it on oneself, to provoke it by one's actions.

clue.text: Hanging over mice and men in disarray

indicators.note: in disarray says the letters of the words before are thrown into disorder and rearranged

explanation.surface: Steinbeck-flavoured scene of mice and men lying in a muddle, with something hanging over them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' is both part of the fodder (MICE + MEN + IN) and the start of 'in disarray'; only 'disarray' signals the anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: Imminence is the state of being about to happen, of a threat looming or impending over someone.

clue.text: No theologian, bishop could be dismissed as surplus to requirements

parts.note: no looks like the letter O, read as nought or nothing
DD is Doctor of Divinity, a theologian's degree
a bishop is a chessman, so a man
in cricket a batsman who is dismissed is out

explanation.surface: Without a scholar of religion, a bishop could lose his job as unnecessary.
explanation.walkthrough: The bishop is a chess piece, giving MAN; 'could be' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The odd one out is the person or thing left over, not needed or not fitting with the rest.

clue.text: Inexperienced soldiers in the intelligence

indicators.note: in places the soldiers inside the word for intelligence

parts.note: gen is British slang for information, the intelligence
RE is the Royal Engineers, a body of soldiers

explanation.surface: New recruits serving in the intelligence corps.
explanation.definitionFit: Green describes someone raw and untrained, like unripe fruit.

clue.text: Tuck possibly produced by cooker, we hear

indicators.note: we hear says the word for a cooker is to be taken as spoken, not as spelt

parts.note: a fryer is a pan or appliance for cooking food in fat

explanation.surface: A school tuck-shop snack turned out by some cooking device.
explanation.walkthrough: Friar Tuck is Robin Hood's portly monk companion; 'Tuck' is not food here. 'possibly' marks him as one example.
explanation.definitionFit: Tuck, the merry monk of the Robin Hood legends, is an example of a mendicant brother.

clue.text: Check condition and replace

parts.note: to rein in is to check or restrain
a state is a condition

explanation.surface: Inspect the state of something and then put it back.
explanation.definitionFit: To reinstate is to restore someone or something to a former place.

clue.text: Dishevelled art models in painting

indicators.note: dishevelled means untidy, so the letters of the words that follow are messed up and rearranged

explanation.surface: Scruffy-looking artists' models posing in a picture.
explanation.definitionFit: An old master is a painting by a great European artist from before about 1800.

clue.text: Threw down club perhaps in shed

definitions.meaning: in card games, getting rid of an unwanted card such as a club by playing it

explanation.surface: Someone flung a golf club down inside a garden hut.
explanation.walkthrough: 'club' is a playing-card suit and 'shed' a verb, not a garden hut; 'in' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Discarding is throwing away an unwanted card, and more generally casting off anything.

clue.text: Exciting runner in night scramble

indicators.note: in puts the runner inside the jumbled letters
a scramble is a jumble, so the letters of night are mixed up

parts.note: a rill is a small stream, something that runs

explanation.surface: A thrilling night-time dash by an athlete.
explanation.walkthrough: 'scramble' is the anagram signal, and 'in' sets the stream inside the rearranged letters. 'runner' suggests an athlete, but in crosswords it is often a watercourse.
explanation.definitionFit: Thrilling means causing a rush of excitement.

clue.text: Game fowls consumed everything, returned about one

indicators.note: consumed means eaten, so the birds take the rest inside them

parts.note: fowls are birds

indicators.note: about places the letters for everything around the one
returned means the word for everything is read backwards

parts.note: all means everything
one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: Game birds that gobbled up everything, then came back round to one spot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returned' reverses the word for everything, 'about' wraps it round the one, and 'consumed' sets that inside the birds. 'Game' suggests shooting birds but is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Billiards is a cue sport played on a cloth-covered table, a game.

clue.text: Flowers for host upset about bereavement

indicators.note: about places the reversed host around the word for bereavement
upset in a down clue means turned upside down, so read backwards

parts.note: a host is a crowd or mob
a bereavement is a loss

explanation.surface: Bouquets sent to a host who is grieving a death.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' turns MOB into BOM; 'host' is a multitude, not someone entertaining guests.
explanation.definitionFit: Blossom is the flowering of a tree or shrub.

clue.text: Slight change of heart for space traveller

indicators.note: a slight change suggests a small shift in the word rather than a full rearrangement, one letter moved

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A small change of mind about wanting to be an astronaut.
explanation.walkthrough: Move the H of HEART from the front to the back. Our planet is the 'space traveller', orbiting the sun.
explanation.definitionFit: Our planet journeys endlessly through the cosmos in its orbit around the sun.

clue.text: An excitable type at the end of the match?

definitions.text: An excitable type at the end of the match?

parts.words: An excitable type at the end of the match?
parts.note: a quick-tempered person, and the burning tip of a struck match

explanation.surface: A rowdy fan at the final whistle of a game.
explanation.walkthrough: 'match' suggests a sports fixture; it is a matchstick, whose head is hot once lit.
explanation.definitionFit: A rash, quick-tempered person is called this, and the lit tip of a matchstick is literally such.

clue.text: Nothing like one's place in the Sahara, say

parts.note: nothing is zero, the letter O
like means as
one's is I'S, one is, written IS

explanation.surface: There is nowhere like your own spot in the desert.
explanation.definitionFit: An oasis is a fertile spot with water in a desert, of which the Sahara is one example.

clue.text: Rope maker supplying girl climbing round top of icefall

indicators.note: round puts the girl around the letter from icefall
climbing in a down clue means going upwards, so read backwards

parts.note: a lass is a girl

indicators.note: top of picks the first letter of icefall

explanation.surface: A girl provides a line while climbing around an ice cliff.
explanation.walkthrough: LASS around I gives LASIS, which 'climbing' turns upward.
explanation.definitionFit: Sisal is a plant fibre from which cord and twine are made.

clue.text: All feet go dancing for this music maker

indicators.note: dancing means moving about, so the letters of the words before are rearranged

explanation.surface: Everyone takes to the floor and dances to this instrument.
explanation.definitionFit: A flageolet is a small wind instrument like a recorder.

clue.text: Pale as was Fagin, say

definitions.meaning: a pale is a stake or palisade
Fagin in Dickens's Oliver Twist received stolen goods

explanation.surface: Asking whether Dickens's villain looked pallid.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pale' looks like an adjective (wan) but is the noun for a stake in a barrier.
explanation.definitionFit: A barrier of stakes is one sense, and a receiver of stolen goods, which Fagin was, is the slang other.

clue.text: Lines in support of sovereign's wear

indicators.note: in a down clue, supporting means placed underneath, so the poem comes below

parts.note: ER is Elizabeth Regina, the sovereign's royal cipher
an ode is a poem, lines of verse

explanation.surface: Poems backing the monarch's clothing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wear' looks like clothing but is the verb, to wear away.
explanation.definitionFit: To erode is to wear away gradually, as water does rock.

clue.text: Bore went to law about smear

indicators.note: about puts the word for went to law around the smear

parts.note: to sue is to go to law, so went to law means sued
a stain is a smear or mark

explanation.surface: A tedious person took someone to court over a slander.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bore' looks like a tedious person (a noun) but is the past tense of bear.
explanation.definitionFit: Bore is the past tense of bear, to endure or support, so held up or endured.

clue.text: Pronounce Peg in Old English

indicators.note: in places the peg inside the abbreviation for Old English

parts.note: a pin is a peg

explanation.surface: Say how to say the name Peg in Anglo-Saxon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pronounce' suggests speech, but here it means to declare an opinion.
explanation.definitionFit: To opine is to state a view, to pronounce on a matter.

clue.text: Falcon pictured as a native of the Mediterranean

definitions.meaning: the falcon pictured on screen is the jewelled bird of the 1941 Humphrey Bogart film noir
someone born on Malta, an island in the Mediterranean

explanation.surface: A bird of prey portrayed as coming from a southern sea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pictured' means in a motion picture: The Maltese Falcon.
explanation.definitionFit: The film title names a statuette bird from Malta, and an islander from Malta has the same name.

clue.text: Doctor went carefully and operated on bed

parts.note: edged means moved slowly and cautiously

explanation.surface: A physician tiptoed in and did surgery on a bed.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'bed' is a riverbed or seabed, not a hospital bed.
explanation.definitionFit: To dredge is to scoop silt from the bottom of a river or harbour, so to work on its floor.
